leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight round-1 configurations name B019 (targeted protein degradation) as the single prize part, which is the only ballot with that many explicit supporters. The shared core is chemically induced proximity between a target and an E3 ligase, with Crews and Deshaies as the conceptual origin. The five differ on the third laureate and on the citation: four (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Zou) name Handa, with citations that include the cereblon/molecular-glue strand, while Aqvist names Ciulli with a PROTAC-only citation about heterobifunctional small molecules. All five record reservations about the absence of an approved degrader and crowded credit; Aili, Aqvist and Zou say these should not block recognition, and Linke (chair) records maturity as a standing reservation. Somfai and Brzezinski list B019 as an alternative, and Sparr lists it as her first alternative, but none of them prefers it in the round-1 configuration.

Somfai prefers Pd-catalysed C-N cross-coupling (Buchwald, Hartwig) on grounds of three decades of independent confirmation, wide use in pharmaceutical and process chemistry, and a compact two-name attribution. He acknowledges that no other member prefers it, that the 2010 cross-coupling prize may be read as covering the same idea, and that the Kosugi and Migita precursor work is unresolved. B019 and B057 are his alternatives.

Sparr prefers ionizable lipid nanoparticles (Cullis, Hope, Anderson) as lipid self-assembly and pKa-tuned phase behaviour turned into a platform with approved products. She states that credit is crowded across Vancouver, Boston and industry, that the overlap with Medicine 2023 is a concern, and that her own field bias may be influencing her; she names B019 and B002 as alternatives and asks whether B019 should be preferred if no approval is required.

Brzezinski prefers long-range electron transfer through proteins (Gray, Winkler) for mechanistic depth, decades of reproduced results and the cleanest two-name attribution. He states that no other member ranked it in their top eight in the opening, that the 1992 Marcus prize may be seen as covering the conceptual core, that Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic priority is unverified, and that his own research is scientifically close to the topic. His alternatives are B046 and B019.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's round-1 configuration is a single prize part, and all eight files state that some reservation applies to their own preferred ballot (maturity, attribution, or prior recognition); nobody presents a first choice as free of weaknesses.

On B019, all five supporters, plus Somfai and Brzezinski who list it as an alternative, accept the same underlying principle (a small molecule that recruits an E3 ligase to a chosen protein, removing rather than inhibiting it) and name Crews and Deshaies as the conceptual origin; the five explicit supporters all include both in their trio.
All eight conflict notes report no personal or institutional tie to any shortlisted candidate; the disclosures concern scientific closeness or colleagueship only.

Several members who do not prefer B002 (nanopore sensing) describe its physical principle and maturity as strong (Aqvist, Chabes, Sparr, Somfai, Zou), while all of them see attribution among Kasianowicz, Branton, Deamer, Bayley and Akeson as the obstacle.
scientific_disputes: Whether targeted protein degradation is one discovery or two: PROTAC-style heterobifunctional design (Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Sakamoto) and cereblon-mediated molecular glues (Handa, Ito, Gray, Kim). Aili, Chabes, Linke and Zou treat them as unified by E3-ligase hijacking; Aqvist, Somfai (in his response to Aili), Brzezinski and Chabes (in his case against) note the strands are distinct and that one citation may not serve both.

Whether the chemistry in degraders is new in kind. Somfai asks what is chemically new; Aili and Zou answer that bifunctional recognition and neo-interaction design is a design principle rather than a new reaction. Linke and Sparr note the ternary-complex cooperativity biophysics is still only partly quantified.

Whether nanopore sensing (B002) is chemistry or biophysics and instrumentation. Somfai and Zou question this; Linke argues the principle is a clear route to a new capability, and the dispute is open since no member prefers B002 in the round-1 configuration.

Whether B055 and B034 extend already recognised work (Marcus 1992; Pd cross-coupling 2010) or add a distinct discovery; B046 (nitrogenase) is described by Brzezinski, Chabes, Zou and Aqvist as secure on structure but unresolved on the N2 reduction mechanism.
attribution_disputes: Third laureate on B019: Handa (Aili, Chabes, Linke, Zou) versus Ciulli (Aqvist). Somfai (in his response to Aqvist) prefers Ciulli over a mixed PROTAC and glue trio but expects a PROTAC-only citation to draw the Handa objection; the files do not show a member who would add Sakamoto, Gray, Ito or Kim to the trio.

Who is the missing name under a cap of three: B019 leaves out Ciulli or Handa plus Sakamoto, Gray, Ito and Kim; B045 involves Cullis, Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Anderson and Langer, with Aili and Sparr proposing different trios (Madden versus Anderson); B002 involves five names with distinct steps (1996 translocation, engineered pores, enzyme ratcheting), and Bayley's role is the specific point raised by Aqvist, Somfai, Zou and Chabes.

Priority claims not settled from the supplied files: Sakamoto's first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies (Aqvist), Kosugi and Migita before Buchwald and Hartwig (Somfai), Dutton, Moser, Beratan and Onuchic on tunnelling pathways (Brzezinski), and Kondo and Nishida for base editing (Aqvist, Chabes).

Similar-looking B019 proposals differ in citation as well as laureates: Aili, Chabes, Linke and Zou cite PROTACs and cereblon, with Chabes and Zou naming cereblon as the target of molecular-glue degraders, while Aqvist limits his citation to heterobifunctional small molecules recruiting an E3 ligase.
maturity_disputes: No member states that a degrader has been approved; several say this from memory only. Somfai, Brzezinski, Sparr and Aqvist treat the missing approval as relevant (Aqvist and Aili reject it as a criterion); Zou, Chabes and Linke ask whether to wait one more year or whether durable clinical efficacy matters.

Sparr and Aqvist's exchange sets B045's approved products and real-world data against B019's late-stage trials; Sparr herself flags the risk that B045 reads as a second pandemic-vaccine prize after Medicine 2023.
Brzezinski and others question whether prior prizes (Marcus 1992, Pd cross-coupling 2010, CRISPR 2020, Medicine 2023) lower the case for B055, B034, B043 and B045 respectively.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Linke (chair), Somfai and Sparr are Lund colleagues; each states this is not a basis for recusal on any shortlisted candidate.

Brzezinski discloses that his research on proton and electron transfer is scientifically close to B055 and that his bias toward the field should be weighed; he also notes that Zou is a Stockholm University colleague, with no bearing on any candidate.
Zou discloses scientific closeness to B005 and B006 (porous materials, electron crystallography); neither is the ballot in his round-1 configuration.

Sparr discloses that her lipid self-assembly research overlaps with B045, her preferred ballot, and describes it as scientific interest rather than a tie to the candidates; Aili notes a self-assembly link to Sparr that does not bear on B019 or B045.
No member discloses a collaboration or institutional tie to any credited candidate.
questions_for_round2: For B019, should the third laureate be Handa or Ciulli, and what specific discovery does each name add that the citation depends on?

Is PROTAC design and cereblon-mediated molecular glue degradation one achievement that can be written in a single citation, or two discoveries that a three-laureate prize cannot honestly combine? If two, is a two-part prize an option?
Is the absence of an approved degrader a reason to defer B019 or not, and what evidence would the committee accept as showing the principle has been delivered?
Can Sparr, Aili or Somfai name a three-person B045 trio that the committee can defend, and does the overlap with Medicine 2023 matter for a Chemistry citation?

If B002 were considered, which single step (translocation, engineered pores, or enzyme-controlled reading) is the discovery, and who would be the three names? Does the committee regard it as chemistry?
Can B034, B055 or any other single-supporter ballot be shown to be a distinct discovery from the earlier prizes it overlaps (2010, 1992), so that it can compete with B019?

Do Brzezinski's, Somfai's and Sparr's alternatives (B019 in each case) represent a willingness to support B019 if the attribution and maturity questions are answered, and what specifically would they need?
summary.chair_observation: B019 is the only ballot with explicit round-1 support from more than one member, and its five supporters are split on one name (four for Handa, one for Ciulli) rather than on the discovery. The other three preferred ballots (B034, B045, B055) each have a single explicit supporter who also states the main weakness of the case. Round 1 does not show a majority position on the laureates or the citation, and the main open points are the PROTAC versus molecular-glue question, the status of clinical approval, and whether other ballots can answer their attribution or prior-prize objections. As chair I note that my own statement described B019 opening support as a top-four placement from all eight members, which overstates the opening ranks (Sparr ranked it sixth and Brzezinski seventh).
